method: tools/parity/oidc-differential.cjs against isolated copies of the API-initialized v2.37.2 fixture, with one ephemeral local RS256 provider; 16 Node-versus-Go cases including web auth, token validation, real-socket event, and mobile PKCE/state behavior
normalization: Random UUIDs, access/refresh tokens, ID tokens, and timestamps are not retained; compare their semantic effects via selected user fields, redirect shape, and session count.
Node and Go use separate copied fixture directories and database files.

JSON object member order is canonicalized for Socket.IO event payload comparison because JSON object order is not semantically significant; array order, scalar values, null versus empty, and the linked user's raw persisted extraData text remain strict.
limits: Compared web auto-registration, provider error, state replay, expired ID token, existing-user email linking, disabled-auto-registration denial, invalid nonce/issuer/audience/signature, and the selected admin-only user_added event.

Compared mobile redirect allowlist rejection, missing and unsupported PKCE method errors, valid S256 authorization parameters, normalized full provider redirect response (status, Location, content type, content length, ETag, and body), full app redirect response, and one-time state consumption/replay including status, content type, content length, ETag, and body.

Detailed callback cookie attributes, expiry of in-memory flow state, mobile app callback/token exchange after the provider code is delivered, additional redirect schemes, and general Socket.IO inventory remain unverified.

Random UUIDs, access/refresh tokens, ID tokens, and timestamps are compared by semantic effect rather than literal values. JSON object member order is canonicalized only for Socket.IO payloads; arrays, scalars, null/empty distinctions, and raw persisted extraData text remain strict.
